open_questions.question: Is 'loose' the right line: any task in no flow or loop, including one written against a spec but created by hand? Operator 2026-11-12: yes.
Is 'piloted' an operator-initiated run, meaning a run started because the operator messaged that agent? Operator 2026-11-12: yes; flow, loop and job runs keep today's moves.
Are done here, done elsewhere (naming a task or commit on main) and cancelled the right set of closes? Operator 2026-11-12: yes.
Should a completed loose task be approvable with no reviewer, or should review stay with an explicit skip? Operator 2026-11-12: approvable with no reviewer.

problem:
Quick fixes are usually hand-made tasks that the operator, or an agent they are directing, tests and then asks to merge. They are held to the same moves a flow's tasks are (task_transitions.py:101-157), and the moves that matter for this way of working are refused. Cases from 2026-11-11 alone:
- F1166: AW-81, AW-82 and AW-83 were built inside AW-80's run and landed with it (477c655). They could not be closed: 'pending' allows only assigned and in_progress. The only exit was a fake build and review of an empty branch, or Delete.
- AW-94 could not be withdrawn before it started: 'pending' to 'rejected' was refused to the agent the operator was directing.
- AW-94 could not be sent straight back after it completed: 'completed' allows only under_review. Taking the detour made the sender its holder for a moment, so the developer's name was lost (api/v1/tasks.py:2471).
- The operator can approve a completed task only through Land, and the board offers no plain cancel.

requirements.rationale: Flows rely on their moves to hand work between builder and checker; loosening them there would break the mechanism the operator says works well. A hand-made task written against a spec is still worked by hand, so it gets the hand moves (operator, 2026-11-12).
requirements.statement: A task is loose when it is not in any flow's or loop's queue, whether or not it is linked to a specification document. Every rule in this document applies only to loose tasks. A task in a flow or loop keeps exactly the moves it has today.
The operator can move a loose task from any status that is not closed to any other status, and can reopen a closed task to pending. Each move is recorded in the task's history with who made it.

requirements.rationale: The operator directs quick fixes through the agent they are talking to; agents running unattended should not gain the same reach (operator, 2026-11-12).
requirements.statement: A run started by the operator's own message (an operator-initiated run, one whose turn carries operator input) can make every move on a loose task that the operator can. A run started by a flow, loop or scheduled job cannot. It keeps today's moves.

requirements.rationale: For quick fixes the operator or the agent they direct has already tested the work; a mandatory reviewer or skip step is ceremony. The project's checks remain the guard (operator, 2026-11-12).
requirements.statement: The operator or a piloted run can approve a completed loose task directly, with no reviewer and no recorded skip. Approving still sends it through the project's landing, checks included.
The operator or a piloted run can send a completed, or approved but not yet landed, loose task straight back to revision. Its holder becomes its builder, never the one who sent it back.
Moving a loose task never makes the mover its holder. The holder changes only when the move names a new holder.

requirements.rationale: Together with approve-and-land (done here) and cancel, this is the complete set of ways a loose task ends (operator, 2026-11-12).
requirements.statement: A loose task can be closed as 'done elsewhere', naming another task or a commit. It is refused unless the named task's work is on main, or the named commit is on main. Once closed, the task's stage is 'on main' at that commit, and no build, check or review runs for it.
A loose task can be cancelled from any status that is not closed, with an optional reason. Nothing of it lands, and its stage is 'closed without landing'.

The operator can select several loose tasks on the board and close all of them in one action, either as done elsewhere by the same task or commit, or as cancelled. A selected task that cannot be closed is named with its reason, and the others still close.
The task drawer offers only the moves the Hub will allow on that task, for whoever is looking, as plain actions. A loose task's actions include approve, send back, close as done elsewhere and cancel.

in_scope: Moves, approval, send-back and closes for tasks in no flow or loop, including hand-made tasks written against a spec
The same moves for operator-initiated agent runs
Plain drawer actions and multi-select close
non_goals: Any change to the moves of tasks in a flow or loop
Giving unattended (flow, loop or job) runs new moves
Deleting tasks; Delete stays as it is
Close outcomes beyond done here (approve and land), done elsewhere and cancelled

summary: A task outside a flow is moved freely by the operator, and by the agent the operator is piloting. It can be approved without a reviewer, sent straight back to its builder, closed as done by another task or commit, or cancelled, singly or several at once. Tasks inside a flow keep today's rules.
